hints: Notice the first peak of the $y$ against $x$ graph is midway between $0$ and $\frac{\lambda}{2}$, at $x = \frac{\lambda}{4}$, with $x = \frac{\lambda}{8}$ on its rising side.
Use symmetry of the sine shape about that peak: an equal height $y_1$ must occur the same distance on the falling side of the peak.
Use periodicity of wavelength $\lambda$: after those two points in the first cycle, the pattern repeats every $\lambda$ in $x$, so add $\lambda$ to the first rising-side position.
walkthrough: Identify the wave shape: $y=0$ at $x=0$, $\lambda/2$, $\lambda$ and so on, so it is a sine wave starting at zero with wavelength $\lambda$ and first crest at $x = \frac{\lambda}{4}$.

The given point $x = \frac{\lambda}{8}$ is $\frac{\lambda}{8}$ to the left of the crest. By symmetry the same displacement $y_1$ occurs $\frac{\lambda}{8}$ to the right of the crest: $x = \frac{\lambda}{4} + \frac{\lambda}{8} = \frac{3\lambda}{8}$.
The wave repeats every $\lambda$ in distance $x$, so every point with displacement $y_1$ recurs at $x + n\lambda$ for integer $n$.
The next rising-side repeat after $x = \frac{\lambda}{8}$ is $x = \frac{\lambda}{8} + \lambda = \frac{9\lambda}{8}$, which comes before the repeat of $\frac{3\lambda}{8}$ at $\frac{11\lambda}{8}$.
Hence in increasing $x$ the next two positions with $y = y_1$ are $\frac{3\lambda}{8}$ and $\frac{9\lambda}{8}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: The value $\frac{5\lambda}{8}$ is past the zero at $\frac{\lambda}{2}$ on the falling negative slope, so displacement there is negative and cannot equal positive $y_1$.

B.explanation: Symmetry about the first peak at $\frac{\lambda}{4}$ gives $\frac{3\lambda}{8}$, and one full wavelength repeat of $\frac{\lambda}{8}$ gives $\frac{9\lambda}{8}$, both with the same $y_1$.

C.explanation: The value $\frac{5\lambda}{8}$ lies in the trough region where $y$ is negative, so it cannot have displacement $y_1$ which is positive.

D.explanation: Both values skip the nearer repeat at $\frac{3\lambda}{8}$ on the falling side of the first peak; $\frac{9\lambda}{8}$ is only the second of the next two positions.
